messages:
sara: Heads-up — vendor just posted a maintenance window that will affect their us-west2 capacity 19:00-22:00 UTC. They called out degraded allocation for GPU-backed dedicated pools. Do we expect impact to any active Dedicated pools or scheduled canaries?
ken: Thanks for flagging. Which vendor? link?
sara: vendorcloud (status: https://status.vendorcloud.example/incidents/1234). Their note says 'reduced availability for GPU instances in us-west2' and possible throttled allocations.
infra-bot: [ALERT] vendorcloud maintenance scheduled 2026-03-20 19:00-22:00 UTC. Affected regions: us-west2. See https://status.vendorcloud.example/incidents/1234
dmitri: If allocations drop we should enable public fallback routing for the small latency-sensitive routes and scale down best-effort workloads. Can someone check reserved pool headroom for us-west2? @ken
ken: On it. Quick look at reserved pools:
```
pool: dedicated-us-west2-a
capacity_total_gpus: 128
allocated_gpus: 96
active_jobs_queue: 7
estimated_headroom: 25% (burst reserve 32 GPUs)
```
ken: There's about ~32 GPUs in burst reserve. If vendor throttles further we may start queuing at peak. No immediate OOM but reduced buffer.
anya: SLA-wise, if we route to hosted models does that change billing or latency SLA for customers on Dedicated? We should notify a small set of customers if we flip routing.
dmitri: Good call. We can enable fallback for the non-enterprise routes first. Config change is just toggle `allow_public_fallback=true` on the routing policy for route-group `interactive-lowlatency`.
sara: Ken — can you run a smoke canary to simulate a 20% spike in token throughput and watch queue delta? Need to know whether we hit the burst reserve.
ken: Running now. Will post quick results in ~5m.
dmitri: Also prep a quick rollout plan: 1) enable fallback on non-enterprise routes, 2) monitor latencies for 10m, 3) if queues < 15% increase keep; else revert and notify. Assign to @ken for step 1/2. :eyes:
ken: Canary done. Output:
```
start: 2026-03-20T18:42:00Z
simulated_spike: +20% token/s
queue_delta: +4 jobs (baseline 7 -> 11)
burst_used: 18/32 GPUs
p99_latency_delta: +28ms
errors: 0
```
ken: So we used ~18 of 32 burst GPUs, queue increased but not catastrophically. p99 latency up ~28ms for canary.
anya: Those numbers seem acceptable for a short window, but notify support and sales for customers with strict latency SLAs.
sara: Agree. Plan: enable fallback for `interactive-lowlatency` at 19:00 UTC, monitor via dashboard (route-level latency + burst usage) and revert if burst reserves drop below 8 GPUs. @ken can you make the toggle and put an annotation in the rollout?
ken: Will do. I’ll push the config toggle and add a rollback watch. Posting the exact command I ran:
```
# enable public fallback for interactive-lowlatency
./infractl routing update --route-group=interactive-lowlatency --set allow_public_fallback=true --annotate "vendor maintenance 2026-03-20"
```
infra-bot: [AUDIT] ken changed routing config for interactive-lowlatency at 2026-03-20T18:55:34Z (annotation: vendor maintenance 2026-03-20)
dmitri: Thx. I'll open a one-line runbook and add the thresholds (burst < 8 GPUs -> rollback). Can someone add a short customer notice draft for support? @anya
anya: On it. Draft in #support in 10m.
sara: Thanks team. If anything changes from vendor side post it here. :thumbsup:
ken: Will keep eyes on metrics and post updates. :rocket:
